meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Common Law for criminal/commercial matters at federal level; Civil Law for private law in Quebec; public law harmonized)

Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Canada Tax Treaties (DTAAs in force with more than 90 jurisdictions)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17; Criminal Code (Canada) R.S.C., 1985, c. C-46, Part XII.2; Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 22; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, S.C. 2011, c. 31; United Nations Act, R.S.C., 1985, c. mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of valid passport (or drivers licence/press photo credential per FINTRAC ID rules) for each individual with significant control
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing national authority in country of origin; notarized by a Quebec notary or equivalent foreign notary commissioner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Canada is party to the Hague Apostille Convention; Apostilles issued by Global Affairs Canada's Authentication Services Section or designated Quebec-based competent authority for Quebec-origin instruments)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address / utility bill and proof of identity for each 10%+ shareholder and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent local authority or utility provider in source jurisdiction; notarized where required by the Registrar
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization where the country of origin is not party to the Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Statutory declaration under oath confirming beneficial ownership and source of funds (Form under Ontario / Quebec depot equivalent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via the Quebec notarial register (Chambre des notaires du Québec) if the declaration is to be used outside Canada; no apostille required for domestic registrations

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / Certificate of incumbency for corporate shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry of the corporate beneficial owner's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization (depending on foreign jurisdiction); English translation by a certified translator may be required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every director, shareholder, UBO, and senior manager against the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) advisory-offences, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals list (subject to Canadian compliance using Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions list), United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, Canadian Criminal Code A designation, and Quebec's Registraire des entreprises denial-of-service list. Under PCMLTFA, a reporting entity must establish a risk-based assessment program, verify client identity, determine if a Politically Exposed Person (PEP) or head of international organization is involved, maintain a transaction/nominating reporting regime to FINTRAC, and report suspicious transactions within 30 days. Record-keeping must persist at least 5 years after the last use or transaction. No named lawyer or accountant privilege applies to UBO disclosure in corporate incorporation instructions, unless genuinely seeking legal advice.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec - Registre des entreprises (https://www.register.quebec.ca) and, for Federal names, Corporations Canada’s Online Filing Centre (http://www.ic.gc.ca/corporations)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11 and QBCA s. 37, the corporate name must be in French. A French version is mandatory for doing business in Quebec. The name must contain a legal element ('Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltée', 'Limitée', or 'Société par actions'). A transliteration from a non-Latin script is permitted only if a certified transliteration into standard French characters is used. The name cannot be identical or confusingly similar to a name already registered in the Quebec enterprise register or a Federal NUANS search. A NUANS report must show green status. If the business intends to operate outside Quebec under a different-language name, an additional or alternative name must be cleared under the applicable foreign registry.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banque, Trust, Fiducie, Insurance, Assurances, Loan, Prêt, Courtier, Broker (unless licensed under OSFI/RAMQ or recognized as a financial institution)

University, Université, College, Collège, Institute, Institut, Medical, Médical, Law Society, Barreau, Ordre, Commission, Tribunal, Court, Cour (requires prior approval from the competent professional regulator or the Registrar)

Royal, Royale, Federated, Fédérale, International, Mondial, Quebec, Québec, Canada, Montréal, Montreal (requires nomenclature approval from a charter authority or the Registrar when implying governmental or official status)
Co-operative, Cooperative, Mutuelle, Union, Syndicate, Syndicat (statutory name restrictions under the cooperatives and syndicates acts)
Pharmacy, Pharmacie, Drug, Drogue, Hospital, Hôpital, Funeral, Funéraire, Transit, Publicité (if false or misleading as to the true activity)
Holdings, Finance, Financial, Capital, Securities, Investissement (only with a clear activity description and prior FINTRAC/securities regulator approval)
Official, Public, Gouvernement, Municipal(e), Souverain, Sovereign, Patrimonial, National, Provincial (without appropriate Crown or ministerial licence)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: When the Registraire des entreprises rejects a name (RAO - 'nom incorrect', 'confusion' or 'interdiction de mention contraire à l'ordre public'), the applicant may: (1) file an administrative objection with the Registraire dans les 30 days under s. 42 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises and ss. 12-13 of the QBCA, providing an amended NUANS report and a corrected name; (2) request a discretionary review by the Chief Mining Inspector? (the correct avenue is a motion for judicial review before the Superior Court of Quebec within 30 days after the final refusal); (3) apply to the Registraire for a formal 'decision de dénomination' after paying the modification fee. For federal names rejected by Corporations Canada, an appeal may be made under s. 41 of the Canada Business Corporations Act (erroneous/likely confusion grounds) with a hearing before the Director and thereafter judicial review in the Federal Court of Canada (application under ss. 18.1 and 18.2 of the Federal Courts Act, RSC 1985, c F-7); a certified NUANS search must accompany the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: In Quebec, a company must maintain a registered office (siège social) in Quebec at a physically accessible address. The address must appear in a public registry and be a place where documents may be served. A virtual office may be permissible if a physical mailbox/service address in Quebec is provided by a licensed service provider and the provider accepts service of process and statutory notices; however, for a retail food-service business (specialty tea salon) the municipal food establishment licence, Québec Restauration sector, and municipal zoning permits entail physical commercial premises and on-site kitchen/service area. Thus, a purely virtual office for the registered office is typically acceptable, but a physical operation location is required for business licensing.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-High (60% within first 6 months of operation). The Régie des alcools, des courses et des jeux (RACJ) or local municipal authorities will conduct a pre-licence inspection to verify zoning, sanitation, food safety, and fire safety. Unannounced spot inspections are common in high-risk food-contact businesses, with an estimated likelihood of 2-3 inspections per 12-month operating year, depending on the municipal by-law and prior food-safety compliance record.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Quebec Business Corporations Act articles of incorporation (transmission to Registraire)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing fee schedule for 'Transmission of articles of incorporation' (approx. CAD $160; converted at 0.75 USD)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registraire's registration certificate and notice of constitutional declaration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed registration fee for the publication of legal persons registration and issuance of a certificate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarized beneficial ownership declaration + notarized ID/address verification bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Quebec notary (Chambre des notaires du Québec) – tariff specified in the Regulation respecting the notarial tariff

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act (Loi sur les sociétés par actions), CQLR c S-31.1 (QBCA), ss. 2, 3, 12-16, 21, 30, 49; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, ss. 2-24; Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11, arts. 63-73. Federal alternative: Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, ss. 5-10.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar), 2050, rue de Bleury, Montréal, QC H3A 2J5; online portal at registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (statuts constitutifs) filed electronically through the Registrar's 'Cliquer pour incorporer' online portal; a notarized deed of incorporation may be used where the incorporators elect a notarial instrument.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the QBCA. Shares must be issued for fair consideration consisting of money, property, or past services; a promissory note or future services are not acceptable consideration (QBCA s. 49). No escrow account or bank blocking is required. Recommended: authorize 1,000 Class A common shares and subscribe them at C$0.10 per share, C$100 fully paid prior to the first banking resolution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Articles of Incorporation filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec be ratified and approved. RESOLVED, that the incorporator's subscription for 1,000 Class A common shares at C$0.10 per share, for total consideration of C$100, be accepted; the shares be allotted and issued as fully paid. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company be fixed at [address], [city], Quebec, and the Registrar of Enterprises be notified accordingly. RESOLVED, that [Name] be and is hereby appointed sole Director, President, and Secretary, with authority to open bank accounts, execute agreements, and complete all statutory filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirmation of Corporate Name and French-Language Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec - online name requisition service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to three proposed corporate names through the Registraire's online name search tool. Each name must satisfy the distinctive, descriptive, and generic requirements of the QBCA and must be usable in French; if the commercial name is in a language other than French, a French-language version must also be registered in accordance with the Charter of the French Language. Retain the name confirmation reference for use in the incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Online name requisition form
Three proposed names in descending order of preference
Consent of any individual whose name appears in the proposed name, if applicable
Payment of name search fee (approximately C$26)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused, amend the proposal or submit alternative names; a formal reconsideration may be requested from the Registraire, and any French-language objection may be cured by registering a compliant French version of the name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles of Incorporation and Payment of Statutory Duties
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec - 'Cliquer pour incorporer' online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online incorporation questionnaire using the confirmed name, authorize 1,000 Class A common shares, appoint the first director, state the initial registered office in Quebec, and pay the C$314 aggregate statutory duties by credit card. The Registrar examines the application and issues a certificate of incorporation upon approval; incorporation takes effect on the date and time certified.
required_dossiers: Name confirmation reference from Step 1
Completed Articles of Incorporation under QBCA s. 3
Declaration of the registered office address
Consent of the first director
Proof of payment of the C$314 statutory duties
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or refused, correct the defects and resubmit the filing electronically; a refusal may be contested by administrative review under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, or by a fresh incorporation application after curing the deficiency.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Automatic Enterprise Registration and Issuance of the Quebec Enterprise Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec, with data exchange to Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Simultaneously with incorporation, file the statement of registration (déclaration d'immatriculation) of the enterprise so that the corporation is registered in the Registre des entreprises. The Registrar assigns the 10-digit Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ), which is required for all subsequent filings with Revenu Québec, CNESST, and municipal authorities. Verify the public registration within 10 days after issuance of the certificate.
required_dossiers: Statement of registration completed within the online incorporation tool
Principal establishment address in Quebec and mailing address
Activity code ISIC 5630 / NAICS 722515
Identity, nationality, and residential address of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration statement contains errors, file an amending declaration (déclaration de modification) online with the Registrar; if registration is delayed, request an attestation of registration from the Registrar and correct any missing data through the online register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of By-Laws, Share Subscription, and Corporate Minute Book
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: The corporation itself acting through its directors, assisted by legal counsel or a notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting, approve the internal by-laws (règlements administratifs), accept the share subscription and issue the Class A share certificate, appoint the sole director as President and Secretary, and open the statutory registers (shareholder register, director register, minutes book) at the registered office in accordance with the QBCA.
required_dossiers: First board resolution in the pro-forma form above
Share subscription forms and proof of payment of C$100
Approved draft by-laws
Class A common share certificate
Minute book and statutory registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any omitted corporate formality may be ratified by a subsequent unanimous shareholder resolution or by a curative by-law; deficient registers may be corrected by signed, dated supplemental entries approved by the directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec (clicSÉQUR Entreprises), Canada Revenue Agency (Business Registration Online), CNESST, and Ville de Montréal permits office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation for QST under the Act respecting the Québec sales tax, for GST/HST under the Excise Tax Act, and as an employer for source deductions, QPIP, QPP, EI, and CNESST workers' compensation. Obtain a municipal commercial operating permit for the tea lounge, and file the mandatory annual updating declaration (déclaration de mise à jour) with the Registraire within 60 days of any change in registered information.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and NEQ
Corporate banking coordinates
Directors' identification and residential details
Payroll estimates and description of income-producing activities
Lease or occupancy document for the principal establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File a correcting application or a late registration through clicSÉQUR or the CRA Business Registration Online portal; request administrative penalty relief from Revenu Québec or the CRA for first-time omissions; ensure all subsequent GST/QST and source-deduction returns are filed on time.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Agriculture, des Pêcheries et de l'Alimentation du Québec (MAPAQ) - Food Establishment Permits Division; municipal authorities through Ville de Montréal Service des permis d'exploitation; Régie du bâtiment du Québec (RBQ) for building occupancy.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Permis d'exploitation d'un établissement alimentaire (MAPAQ Food Establishment Operating Permit) and municipal business operating permit (permis d'exploitation) for a tea salon and food-service lounge.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) - Direction de l'évaluation environnementale
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category D (declaration of compliance) or exemption under the Regulation respecting the environmental impact assessment and review of certain projects (CQLR c Q-2, r. 23.1); a specialty tea salon without a manufacturing process does not require a full impact assessment but must obtain municipal plumbing and grease-trap approvals and comply with municipal waste-management by-laws.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with municipal sanitary sewer by-laws and the Regulation respecting wastewater discharge, including maximum concentrations for BOD5, total suspended solids, and fats, oils, and grease; install and maintain a suitably sized grease interceptor for all food-preparation sinks; ensure kitchen exhaust ventilation does not create odors or VOC nuisances beyond municipal by-law limits; comply with Quebec's organic waste treatment ban by sorting and directing food residues to authorized biomethanation or composting facilities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the competent municipal fire service (Service de sécurité incendie) verifying compliance with Part 3 of the Quebec Construction Code; electrical installation clearance by the Corporation de maîtrise en électricité du Québec (CME); municipal certificate of occupancy (certificat d'occupation) for food-service use; accessibility compliance under the Quebec Building Code; and CNESST workplace health and safety clearance for staff areas.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Revenu Québec; federal portal: Canada Revenue Agency My Business Account; Quebec portal: Revenu Québec CléNuméro / Mon Dossier d'entreprise
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity carrying on business in Canada or Quebec must obtain a federal Business Number (BN) via the CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) service, and a Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) plus GST/HST, QST, and payroll accounts via Revenu Québec's Registraire d'entreprise and online services. The Canadian corporation must file articles of incorporation (federal or provincial), obtain a federal BN program account (RC0001 for corporate income tax), register for GST/HST (RT0001) if taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 or voluntarily, and register for Quebec QST if taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000; a non-resident corporation must designate a representative for service of process and may need a Section 216 election for deemed dispositions. A foreign entity without a permanent establishment in Canada may be required to obtain a TIN by filing Form RC4150 (Application for a Canada Revenue Agency Business Number for Non-Residents) or by direct registration at a CRA tax services office.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) status elections for small business deduction under ITA s. 125; federal-provincial allocation via permanent establishment rules; Quebec QST and GST/HST combined filing election; non-resident corporation election under ITA s. 216 for rental income or timber royalties; s. 85 rollover elections for incorporation; hybrid mismatch rules under BEPS Action 2 not applicable as Canada has not implemented a general hybrid mismatch election, but specific anti-avoidance rules under ITA s. 245 and Part VI.1 apply; available check-the-box equivalent is the corporate status election for partnership or joint venture; Quebec allows a voluntary registration election for GST/HST and QST; no general check-the-box regime exists in Canada, but a non-resident can elect under ITA s. 219 to file a branch tax return.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) and QST (Quebec Sales Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 per calendar quarter for GST/HST; Quebec QST threshold also CAD 30,000, but once a business exceeds CAD 30,000 in taxable supplies in a single calendar quarter, registration is mandatory and becomes effective from the day of the triggering supply; for non-residents making taxable supplies to Canadian consumers, digital economy registration may apply with no threshold for certain supplies if subject to the simplified GST/HST registration regime. Physical presence nexus in Quebec: a permanent establishment in Quebec requires QST registration regardless of threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No federal/Quebec real-time electronic fiscal clearance mandate for general B2C invoices; GST/HST and QST invoice must contain supplier name, BN/QST registration number, date of invoice, description, and tax amounts. Quebec mandates electronic payment remittance through Revenu Québec's Transmission électronique for certain remitters; digital service providers must use the e-file (fichier électronique) via Revenu Québec's online portal; CRA requires electronic filing of GST/HST returns for registrants with annual taxable supplies exceeding CAD 1.5 million; no mandatory digital stamping, API clearance, or real-time fiscal server posting; however, Quebec has an electronic invoicing pilot (e-invoicing) under the Conseil du trésor, but not compulsory for private B2C tea lounges. CRA requires that books and records be kept in Canada or be available electronically on request; no per-invoice government fiscal clearance is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods are zero-rated under GST/HST (s. 123 and Schedule VI, Part V) when the supplier ships the goods directly outside Canada and maintains evidence of export within the required time; services supplied to non-residents (except certain services performed in Canada, services to a non-resident who is registered, or services relating to real property in Canada) may be zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part V and s. 7; Quebec QST zero-rating mirrors the GST/HST for exports under QST Act (s. 185 and Schedule VI); a specialty tea salon exporting packaged loose-leaf tea, tea ceremony equipment, or ceramic wares to non-resident customers must show that the goods are delivered outside Canada by common carrier, courier, or mail, or that the purchaser is a non-resident and the goods are exported within a reasonable time. For B2B zero-rated services, the supplier must maintain the recipient's non-resident status evidence and the service must be performed wholly outside Canada or be an excluded service under Schedule VI. Refund mechanism: net tax calculation includes input tax credits (ITCs) or ISCs (Quebec input tax refunds) for embedded GST/QST, and zero-rated exporters can claim full input tax credits; the foreign supplier may apply for a rebate under s. 252 of the Excise Tax Act for tax paid on imported goods/services used in commercial activities; the rebate application is Form GST189.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) export report / Form B13A, or annual export reporting through the Canadian Export Reporting System (CAED) for goods exported from Canada)
Bill of Lading or transport document showing shipment from Canada to the foreign destination
Packing list or invoice evidencing commercial terms and foreign buyer identity
Proof of foreign payment (bank transfer, SWIFT, credit card settlement, or Inward Remittance Certificate from the Canadian bank)
CBSA Option 15 or Customs Self-Assessment documentation for low-value shipments
Courier or postal service tracking record demonstrating export within 60 days (GST/HST policy P-051) or applicable CRA administrative tolerance
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may deny input tax credits and reassess zero-rated exports if documentary evidence is insufficient; penalties under Excise Tax Act (ETA) s. 285: failure to provide information (CAD 250 per day, minimum CAD 1,500); false statements or omissions: greater of CAD 250 and 5% of the tax, increased to 10% for repeat violations; gross negligence penalty under ETA s. 285.1: up to 50% of the net tax amount or 25% of the available rebate; fraudulent export claims may trigger criminal prosecution under the Criminal Code, a fine of up to CAD 200,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years; QST penalties under the Act respecting the Québec sales tax, s. 121-124 allow penalties of 25% of the evaded tax plus interest. Retroactive clawback period: CRA may reassess within 3 years for ordinary cases, 4 years (Quebec), and without time limit in cases of misrepresentation or fraud (ETA s. 298; QST Act s. 83).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (central monetary authority); Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) (prudential regulation of federally-chartered banks); Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) (Quebec financial sector regulation); Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) (AML/CFT supervision of reporting entities)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a fully convertible currency under a free-floating exchange rate regime. There are no exchange controls or restrictions on current account transactions, capital account movements, or profit remittances under federal or Quebec law. Dividends, interest, royalties, and management fees may be remitted to non-resident shareholders or affiliates without prior central bank approval, provided that applicable Part XIII non-resident withholding taxes under the Income Tax Act (Canada) are satisfied and the remitting corporation is duly compliant with Quebec Revenue Agency (Revenu Québec) requirements. No material convertibility hurdles exist; however, the source-of-funds and beneficial-ownership verification requirements imposed by domestic banks and FINTRAC constitute practical gateways for cross-border remittances.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada does not impose statutory export proceeds surrender rules or mandatory conversion ratios. Exporters are free to retain foreign currency in foreign or domestic bank accounts. Nonetheless, exporters must (i) report goods and services trade data under the Customs Act and the Canadian International Merchandise Trade statistics program administered by Statistics Canada, (ii) maintain records sufficient to reconcile export proceeds for tax purposes, and (iii) comply with FINTRAC reporting thresholds for large cross-border currency movements and electronic funds transfers. No CAD conversion mandate applies to export receipts of the specialty tea salon lounge.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Chequing) and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account (Business Chequing) and Sweep Account
Operational Account and Credit Facility Settlement Account
Operational Account and FX/Trade Settlement Account
Operational Account and Liquidity Reserve Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility with material legal constraints. Non-bank offshore financial technology entities and electronic money institutions (EMIs) are not considered 'banks' under the Bank Act (Canada) and cannot accept deposit liabilities in the ordinary course of a retail banking business. Offshore EMIs may operate lawfully in Canada only as Money Services Businesses (MSBs) or Foreign Money Services Businesses (FMSBs) registered with FINTRAC, and in Quebec may require a licence under the Act respecting money-services businesses administered by the AMF. Such entities can provide payment facilitation, foreign exchange conversion, and cross-border disbursement rails, but they are not eligible to hold corporate escrow balances or provide government-guaranteed CDIC deposit protection. Accordingly, reliance on EMIs is acceptable as a secondary payments rail; the primary treasury relationship must rest with a Schedule I domestic bank or a Quebec-licensed financial institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, Schedule I Canadian banks and Quebec-based Desjardins require at least one director, officer, or authorized signing representative with Canadian presence to complete a face-to-face identity verification interview at a branch or via a bank-approved notarized identity attestation. Full remote opening is generally not available for newly incorporated corporations with non-resident directors or shareholders; enhanced due diligence will mandate a physical or notarized meeting, certified true copies of passports, corporate registry extracts from Corporations Canada or the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), and a source-of-funds declaration. The Quebec jurisdiction is especially rigorous in requiring proof of the beneficial owner structure and a registered office within Quebec. Remote opening is only feasible where the bank maintains an existing relationship and the corporate UBO has a verifiable Canadian credit and compliance history.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Undisclosed or opaque ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) chain involving non-resident shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete corporate register extract from Corporations Canada or REQ, Register of Individuals with Significant Control, notarized passports of all UBOs, an annotated ownership chart, and a signed declaration of control confirming no nominee or shell concealment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient source of funds for initial capital injection or shareholder loan
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Personal and corporate bank statements covering the prior 12 months, tax assessments or notices of assessment from the Canada Revenue Agency and Revenu Québec, audited or reviewed financial statements, board resolution authorizing the injection, and gift or loan agreements duly notarized.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive specialty retail revenue profile causing transaction monitoring alerts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Point-of-sale terminal settlement reports, daily sales summaries, inventory purchase invoices from tea and ceramics suppliers, GST/HST and QST remittance reconciliations, and a written cash-management policy demonstrating daily deposit discipline.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk country exposure through cross-border tea import supply chains
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid customs entry documents (Form B3), commercial invoices, bills of lading, certificates of origin, supplier due diligence questionnaires, and evidence of compliance with the Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) import requirements for tea products.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident director or shareholder with limited Canadian nexus
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized cross-border identity verification, visa or resident status documentation, professional reference letters from an existing bank or regulated financial institution, a power of attorney granted to a Canadian-resident authorized agent, and a corporate governance charter validating board authority.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity subscriptions, shareholder loan advances, and intra-group funding must be routed through a Canadian Schedule I bank or a Quebec-licensed caisse using SWIFT MT103 wire instructions. The remitter must reference the correct Canadian cross-border payment purpose code, typically 'Direct Investment — Equity' or 'Direct Investment — Intercompany Loan' as defined under Statistics Canada's Classification of Outward and Inward Direct Investment. For Quebec corporate filings, the wire narrative must include the REQ enterprise number and the business corporation 'legal name' exactly as registered. The receiving bank will verify the source of funds, UBO structure, and authorization matrix before crediting the capital escrow or operating account. Payments exceeding CAD 10,000 in a single transaction are reportable to FINTRAC where cross-border electronic funds transfer thresholds are met. For tea salon operations, inbound injections are normally routed as CAD-denominated wires to avoid FX slippage, with FX conversion performed at the receiving bank at the prevailing wholesale rate.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlement for imported loose-leaf tea, ceramic teaware, and cultural inventory is executed via (i) SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier wire payments, (ii) commercial letters of credit (sight or usance) for bulk procurement where the supplier requires documentary protection, and (iii) Payments Canada Lynx same-day large-value settlement for domestic water transfers in CAD. For sub-CAD-clearing-value payments, the Real-Time Rail (RTR) and Interac e-Transfer rails are permissible for local vendors, utilities, and Quebec service providers. Outbound USD or foreign-currency disbursements are coordinated through the bank's FX desk under an executed master FX agreement. All outbound payments must comply with the bank's sanctions screening and FATF recommendations; trade documents must be retained for six years under Quebec record-keeping standards.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla FX forwards for CAD/USD and CAD/CNY trade settlement
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted only when executed through a Canadian Schedule I bank or a regulated derivatives dealer, used primarily for inconvertible counterparty currencies
Cross-currency swaps with a licensed Canadian financial institution for long-term intercompany funding and profit repatriation hedging
FX options (plain-vanilla puts and calls) for premium protection on material tea import invoices

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration de mise à jour) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Québec Enterprise Registrar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based deadline: within 60 days after the annual registration anniversary (date of incorporation/registration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for two consecutive years authorizes administrative strike-off (dissolution); certificates of compliance become unavailable; directors may be held personally liable for unpaid registration costs; fines may be imposed under Quebec publicity legislation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) - required if the corporation is federally incorporated and registered extra-provincially in Quebec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based deadline: within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing for two consecutive years may trigger administrative dissolution; Certificate of Compliance withheld; summary-conviction fines up to CAD 5,000 may apply to offending directors/officers.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined general (Federal 15% + Quebec 11.5%); 12.2% combined for a Canadian-controlled private corporation eligible for the federal small business deduction (9%) and the Quebec SMB reduced rate (3.2%) on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal Small Business Deduction (SBD) reduces effective federal rate to 9% on active business income up to the business limit; Quebec SMB reduced rate of 3.2% applies to the same base; additional Quebec investment tax credits, innovation credits, and regional incentives may apply for a specialty tea lounge with physical business premises and qualifying R&D or training expenses

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return; electronic filing via CRA 'My Business Account' or approved E-file software (EFA/EFU); paper filing accepted but discouraged
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing due 6 months after taxation year-end (e.g., Dec 31 fiscal year-end -> June 30). Payment balance-due date: 3 months after year-end for a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) claiming the SBD; 2 months for other corporations

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered corporation legal name, CRA business number (BN), mailing address, taxation year-end
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Canadian corporation's name and BN; non-resident shareholders are not filers but dividend withholdings must be reported separately

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate revenue from loose-leaf tea sales, lounge food and beverage service, ceramic retail, and other operating revenue
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all gross sales on an accrual basis; include GST/HST charged but excluded in revenue lines

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening inventory, purchases of tea leaves, ceramics, food/beverage supplies, closing inventory
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Follow year-end physical inventory count and consistency with T2 Schedule 1 (supplementary financial data)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after adjustments, capital cost allowance, and deduction of prior-year non-capital losses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Applies to the Canadian resident corporation; no line-level instructions for non-resident shareholders

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net federal Part I tax after the small business deduction and any investment tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No direct non-resident participation in line computation; shareholder residency influences Part XIII withholding on dividends paid

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of the balance due plus 1% per full month, max 12 months; repeat failures increase to 10% plus 2% per month. Late payment interest accrues at CRA prescribed rates (quarterly). Failure to file electronically when required can result in an additional penalty of CAD 100. Gross negligence penalty: 50% of tax understatement.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Quebec Corporation Income Tax Return (CO-17) filed via Revenu Quebec's 'Mon dossier d'entreprise' or approved electronic transmission software
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing due within 6 months of the Quebec taxation year-end, aligned with the federal fiscal year. Quebec balance-due date is 3 months after year-end for a qualified SME (PME); generally 2 months for other corporations

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporation's legal name and Quebec enterprise number (NEQ); official address and mailing address
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Canadian corporation's NEQ; non-resident shareholders do not complete this section

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income computed under Quebec rules, generally reconciled to federal taxable income with provincial adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Align with T2 reconciliation schedules; non-residents are not excluded from the calculation but do not file this return

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec taxable income after provincial loss carryovers and special deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Same source federal amount; no separate non-resident adjustment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provincial corporate tax computed at the applicable rate (general 11.5% or SME reduced rate 3.2%)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders do not take this line; this is the operating corporation's tax obligation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 270 – Net Quebec tax after credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable after refundable and non-refundable credits (e.g., new business tax credits, investment credits)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No non-resident instructions beyond corporate residency requirement

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty under the Quebec Tax Administration Act: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month, up to 12 months, increased to 10% plus 2%/month for second or subsequent failures within a 5-year period. Interest is charged as a percentage of unpaid tax daily at the prescribed rate. Assessment may also include the federal 50% gross negligence penalty on federal recalculations.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% on gross taxable dividends paid or deemed paid by a Canadian resident corporation to a non-resident of Canada, applied under Part XIII of the federal Income Tax Act
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced treaty withholding rate, the non-resident beneficial owner must deliver to the Canadian payer a completed CRA Form NR301 (Declaration of Eligibility for Benefits Under a Tax Convention for a Withholding Rate Reduction) along with a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) and taxpayer identification number issued by the foreign treaty jurisdiction. The form must be received before the dividend payment date to reduce withholding at source. Where the full 25% was withheld, the non-resident may apply to the CRA using Form NR7 (Application for Refund of Non-Resident Tax Paid) within the applicable limitation period—generally two years from the end of the calendar year of withholding—subject to treaty deadlines; a separate Quebec refund application may be necessary if provincial portions are involved.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory federal withholding rates: royalties or amounts paid for the production or reproduction of intellectual property, know-how or film/TV rights: 25%; interest paid to non-residents that is not arm's length or payable in Canadian currency: 25%; arm's length interest paid to unrelated foreign lenders on approved debt is generally exempt. Treaty relief under the Canada-US Convention: royalties commonly reduced to 10% (or 0% for certain comparable rights), interest is generally exempt if arm's length and not related to a permanent establishment under the 2007 protocol; other treaties may reduce both to 10% or provide lower rates.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CRA requires contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation for cross-border transactions with non-arm's length parties where transaction values exceed CAD 5,000,000 in the fiscal period for goods, services, interest and intangible rights; or CAD 7,500,000 for capital transactions. No mandatory Local File/Master File regime applies to small corporations, but OECD-aligned financial records are prudent for groups with global consolidated revenue in excess of CAD 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no separate ESR (Economic Substance Regulations) file; the business purpose doctrine and the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) under ITA s.245 apply to disregard transactions or arrangements lacking a genuine commercial objective. A specialty tea salon lounge will satisfy substantive requirements through a physical service location, full-time personnel, tea inventories, customer contracts, utilities, and a valid business licence. Structuring the corporation solely as a treaty-shopping vehicle or maintaining offshore accounts without operational backing will expose it to GAAR adjustments, interest, and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / False or Misleading Statements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly omitting cash sales from payroll or tax returns, inflating expenses, using point-of-sale suppression software ('zapper' software), failing to file the T2 or CO-17 within the 6-month window, or inducing penalties by presenting fabricated documentation to the CRA/Revenu Quebec
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Gross negligence penalty under ITA s.163(2) of 50% of the tax understated; late-filing penalties of 5% plus 1% per month up to 12 months; criminal prosecution under Criminal Code s.380(1)(a) for fraud over CAD 5,000, which is an indictable offence in Canada, also covered by Quebec's Tax Administration Act anti-evasion measures; maximum prison sentence up to 14 years for criminal fraud; fines without limitation; additional civil penalties at both federal and provincial levels
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where the corporation is insolvent or fails to pay source deductions (payroll, GST/HST), directors may be jointly and severally liable under ITA s.227.1 and Quebec corresponding provisions if due diligence defence fails. Criminal conviction can result not only in monetary fines and imprisonment but also travel restrictions during court proceedings and professional disqualification. Courts may order restitution and issue departure bans pending trial.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating a Canadian corporation with no real employees, no physical shop, no customer turnover, and no economic substance solely to divert profits to a lower-tax foreign affiliate; charging non-arm's length royalties for tea trademarks or management fees at non-arm's-length prices to strip profits from the Canadian operations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR recharacterization: CRA may disallow the benefit and reassess tax as though the arm's-length result had occurred; transfer-pricing penalties under ITA s.247(3) for failing to use arm's length terms: penalty equal to 10% of the net adjustment (reduced to 5% if reasonable efforts demonstrated); interest and compounding on reassessed tax; denial of loss carryovers and retroactive reassessment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors knowingly approving a sham structure may be jointly liable with the corporation under s.160 for unpaid taxes resulting from the adjusted income; in criminal fraud scenarios, personal assets can be reached through civil actions, and restrictions on leaving Canada may be sought to secure attendance. Directorial good faith is not a defence if the arrangement is fraudulent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Record-Keeping and Source Deduction Failures
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to keep adequate books and records for the tea salon (invoice stubs, hotel/restaurant revenue journal, cash register roll, inventory counts, tip allocations, and contracts); failure to remit GST/HST and payroll source deductions; commingling personal and corporate funds; refusing to provide access to electronically generated POS data after request
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under ITA s.230(7), failure to keep books and records: CAD 1,000 to CAD 8,000 fine and possible imprisonment up to 6 months (for each offense); under the Excise Tax Act, failure to remit GST/HST: penalty equal to 6% of the unremitted amount plus daily interest at prescribed rates; Quebec may impose additional fines for co-extensive failures; tax withholding omissions trigger director liability for unremitted amounts with recovery directly from corporate assets, and standard bank/lockbox seizure powers
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors or officers who fail to deduct, withhold, remit, or pay GST/HST or source deductions are jointly and severally liable for the required amounts; if the corporation is wound up without settlement, the directors may be personally assessed without transient immunities; imprisonment may be ordered for chronic non-remittance under the Excise Tax Act for willful evasion; civil recovery may include seizure of personal assets and restrictions on travel or bank accounts in support of tax collection.
